summary: Foreword to the Sales and Use Tax Regulations; defines terms, not a taxability rule.
Charges for services per se are generally not taxable; the service provider is the consumer of property used incidentally.
Custom programming, electronically delivered software, and data processing services are generally not taxable; prewritten software on tangible media is taxable.
Meals and food products furnished to patients/residents of hospitals and qualifying care facilities are exempt.
Transfers of mailing lists are generally taxable like tangible personal property; one-time-use lists are treated as nontaxable services.
Funeral directors are retailers of caskets, vaults, and similar tangible goods; such sales are taxable.
Fees for professional services (e.g., licensed architects) are not taxable; the provider is the consumer of tangible items used.
Amounts for the patent/copyright interest under a technology transfer agreement are not taxable; only the tangible property portion is taxed.
A construction contract with a customer is generally not a taxable retail sale; contractors pay tax on materials they consume and are retailers of fixtures.
Retail sales by manufacturers of tangible personal property are taxable on the full gross receipts.
Sales of machinery, tools, and supplies used in manufacturing are taxable; materials physically incorporated into the product are purchased for resale and not taxed.
Charges for fabricating or processing tangible personal property using customer-furnished materials are taxable.
Charges for making original recordings and qualified master tapes are largely not taxable; tax applies to the sale price of the tangible recording media.
Sales of photographs and photocopies are taxable, whether or not made to the customer's special order.
Charges for qualified motion picture production services and the right to exploit a film are not taxable; producers are consumers of raw materials.
Tax applies to 55 percent of receipts from coke sold to foundries (the portion consumed in the process).
Dyestuffs and listed chemicals that become a component of furs sold by fur dressers and dyers are not taxable (purchased for resale).
Teleproduction/postproduction service equipment qualifies for a partial sales tax exemption; the remaining state/local rate still applies.
Qualified LPG used in agriculture or for household activity in a qualified residence is exempt.
Off-road commercial timber harvesting equipment qualifies for a partial exemption; the balance of the rate still applies.
Racehorse breeding stock qualifies for a partial sales tax exemption; the remaining rate still applies.
Advertising agency and commercial artist services are not taxable; transfers of finished art as tangible personal property are taxable.
Sales of printing and printed matter are generally taxable.
Sales of printed publications are taxable; author manuscript services are not taxable.
Separately stated repair and installation labor is not taxable; parts and materials furnished are taxable.
Sales of retreaded/recapped tires are taxable; for a lump-sum charge, 75 percent is treated as the taxable sales price.
Fur sold in connection with repairing/altering/remodeling is taxable; separately stated repair labor is not.
Materials, parts, and fabrication by reupholsterers are taxable; separately stated repair labor is not.
Lump-sum charges for repainting or refinishing used articles are not taxable; the refinisher is the consumer of the materials.
For many miscellaneous lump-sum repair operations the repairer is the consumer of materials; separately stated parts and finished goods sold are taxable.
Auctioneers making retail sales are retailers; gross receipts from auction sales are taxable.
Retail sales of vehicles by dealers are taxable; tax/use tax is generally collected through the DMV.
Sales of tangible personal property by banks and insurance companies (non-exempt) are taxable, as are sales to them.
Retail sales of beer, wine, and liquor are subject to sales tax (measured on a price that includes alcoholic beverage excise taxes).
A consignee or lienor selling tangible personal property is a retailer; such sales are taxable.
Sales of tangible personal property by charitable organizations are generally taxable unless a specific statutory exemption applies.
Retail sales by florists are taxable; special sourcing rules apply to florist-to-florist (wire) orders.
Sales of headstones, monuments, and other memorial tangible goods are taxable.
Court-ordered sales, foreclosures, and repossession sales of tangible personal property are generally taxable retail sales.
Sales of merchandise through vending machines are generally taxable, with special measure rules for food products.
Sales of modular systems furniture are taxable, with special measure rules for certain installation/assembly.
Membership fees are taxable when they are part of the price of, or required to make, sales of tangible personal property.
Retail sales of cellular phones and wireless devices are taxable; bundled phones are taxed on the unbundled sales price.
Retail sales of works of art are taxable, with limited exemptions for certain pieces acquired for public museum display.
Feed, drugs, and medicines for animals that will be sold as food (and food animals) are exempt; pets, pet food, and supplies are taxable.
Seeds, annual plants, and fertilizer whose products will be sold as food are exempt; ornamental and non-food items are taxable.
Nonreturnable containers sold with their contents, and containers sold with exempt contents, are generally not separately taxable.
Retail sales of newspapers and periodicals are generally taxable, with limited exemptions for certain subscription and nonprofit publications.
Medicines dispensed under a valid prescription are exempt; over-the-counter medicines are generally taxable.
Prescription eyeglasses and ophthalmic materials furnished to patients are generally not taxable to the patient; the dispensing practitioner is the consumer.
Sales of aircraft and parts are generally taxable, with exemptions for common carriers, foreign/interstate use, and certain operators.
Sales of watercraft are generally taxable, with limited exemptions (e.g., commercial deep-sea fishing, certain interstate use).
Occasional sales, such as a one-time sale of used personal property by someone not in the business of selling, are generally exempt.
Buildings and property affixed to real property are generally treated as real property, not taxable tangible personal property.
Certain transfers by qualifying nonprofit organizations (e.g., specified relief, museum, or thrift situations) are exempt from tax.
Sales of motor vehicle and aircraft fuels are subject to sales tax (with prepayment rules); fuel excise taxes are separate.
Retail sales of coins are generally taxable; bulk sales of monetized bullion above the statutory threshold may be exempt.
Sales of food products for human consumption (groceries for home consumption) are generally exempt.
Sales of hot prepared food and meals furnished by restaurants and similar establishments are taxable.
Sales of vehicles, vessels, and aircraft are taxable; use tax on private-party sales is generally collected by the DMV.
Sales to the United States and its instrumentalities are exempt from California sales tax.
Retail sales within federal areas located in California are generally subject to California sales and use tax.
Addresses whether federal taxes are included in the measure of tax; a computation rule, not a product taxability rule.
Sales made to the United States under qualifying government supply contracts are generally exempt.
Qualifying sales to foreign missions and consuls holding valid exemption cards are exempt.
Sales of goods shipped by the retailer to an out-of-state destination are generally not subject to California sales tax.
Sales to common carriers are generally taxable, subject to specific exemptions for property used in interstate/foreign commerce.
Separately stated delivery charges by common carrier from the retailer to the customer are generally not taxable.
Addresses the measure of tax for goods damaged in transit; a measure/procedural rule.
Separately stated charges by packers, loaders, and shippers for their services are generally not taxable.
Title not cleanly parsed; treat as procedural/charge-handling rule pending review.
Credit sales and repossessions; a measure/procedural rule rather than a product taxability rule.
Bad debt deductions; a procedural/relief rule, not a product taxability rule.
Treatment of separately stated debit card charges; a measure/procedural rule.
Barter, exchange, and trade-ins; a measure rule for how the taxable amount is computed.
Returns, defects, and replacements; a procedural rule for adjusting tax, not a product taxability rule.
The lease or rental of tangible personal property to a consumer is generally subject to California sales/use tax.
Leases of mobile transportation equipment are taxable, generally measured by the lessor's purchase price unless an election is made.
Exemption certificates; a procedural/documentation rule.
Sales of property purchased for resale, supported by a valid resale certificate, are not taxable.
Demonstration/display use of resale inventory; a use-tax procedural rule.
Gifts, marketing aids, premiums, and prizes; addresses who owes tax on promotional items, not consumer product taxability.
Trading stamps and promotional plans; a retailer-side measure/procedural rule.
Collection of use tax by retailers; an administrative/nexus rule.
Payment of use tax by purchasers; an administrative rule.
Receipts for tax paid to retailers; a documentation rule.
Information returns; a reporting/procedural rule.
Recordkeeping requirements; an administrative rule.
Seller's permits; an administrative/registration rule.
Reimbursement for sales tax (passing tax to the customer); a procedural rule.
Tax-paid purchases resold; a credit/procedural rule.
Successor's liability; an administrative/collection rule.
Interest and penalties; an administrative rule.
Whole-dollar reporting; a computation/reporting rule.
Relief from liability; an administrative rule.
Drop shipments are taxable retail sales; the drop shipper may be liable as the retailer when the true retailer is not registered in California.
Electronic funds transfer; a payment/procedural rule.
